integration_questions: At 0.18 m track, does the robot still turn sharply enough on the slalom, or does line loss rise at the tightest bends compared with 0.16 m?
Which kp and kd range is stable at this track width, and does the oval still finish reliably?
On which track and at what course position does max_error peak, and does line loss occur at that same point?
Are the outer sensors (x = +/-0.06 m) carrying much signal, and could their weights be reduced to lower slalom line loss?
feedback_request.requested_format: Brief notes on each question, plus the single geometry change you would make first if you could change only one thing.

intent: Continue the single-variable wheel-track sweep from iteration 5 by moving wheel_track from 0.16 to 0.18 m (the upper limit of the allowed range). Keep the seven-sensor, +/-0.06 m span, 16 mm footprint, y = 0.06 m, 0.6 kg, 0.03 m radius and 0.16 x 0.12 m body fixed so the effect is attributable. Expect a score at or above 546 from fewer bend overshoots on the s-bend, with the slalom still unfinished.
learning: Track width is monotonic so far: 0.10 m (357) < 0.12 m (483) < 0.14 m (517) < 0.16 m (546). Hypotheses: (1) 0.18 m continues the trend with diminishing returns; (2) the oval and slalom turn authority falls off past 0.16 m, so the score peaks; (3) the slalom needs a sensing change (footprint or span) because it has never finished in any iteration. Measurements to request on each development track: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort.
rationale: Iteration 5 (wheel_track 0.16 m, all else as iteration 1) is the best design so far at 546.1. Across the clean single-variable sweep, score rises monotonically with track width: 0.10 m gave 357.3, 0.12 m gave 482.7, 0.14 m gave 517.1 and 0.16 m gave 546.1. The gains are shrinking (+125, +35, +29), so the trend is flattening but has not reversed. Every bend failure is still an off-track end with max_error at or above 0.06 m, while rms_error stays at 0.021 to 0.031 m. The problem is occasional large excursions, not steady tracking error. Oval finishes fell from 20/20 at 0.14 m to 18/20 at 0.16 m, so the oval has started to suffer. Body width cannot widen the off-track limit (max(0.06, 0.0125 + width/4) stays at 0.06 m), so that lever is closed. Sensing changes were confounded in iteration 2, so I will not change sensing again yet. I will keep the iteration 5 layout and change only wheel_track, from 0.16 to 0.18 m, to test whether the trend continues. Expected result: s-bend finishes at or above the 0.16 m rate (10/20), a score at or above 546, and the slalom still at or near zero finishes. Main risk: the robot may turn too slowly for the slalom's tightest bends and the oval may keep losing finishes. If the score falls, the optimum is near 0.16 m and the next iteration should test sensor footprint (0.012 m) or span.
